title: With the threads and gevent pools a revoke or an expiry does not stop a task that waits in the pool: it runs and its SUCCESS replaces REVOKED
where: no upstream thread found (searched revoke threads pool, revoke gevent, revoked task still executed, revoke prefetched task; closest celery issue 10490, about terminate and shutdown on the threads pool, and celery issue 4300, ETA); not in the tracker yet
observed: 768e476 with kombu 445027e, redis-py 8.1.0, Redis 7 broker and backend, one worker -c 1, acks_late, A runs 4 s and B waits behind it, revoke(B) 1 s later, nothing injected: threads 2 of 2 and gevent 2 of 2 ran B ("Tasks flagged as revoked" logged, B ended SUCCESS); prefork 2 of 2 and solo 2 of 2 discarded it (REVOKED). With expires=2 on B instead of a revoke: threads 2 of 2 ran B after it expired, prefork 2 of 2 discarded it. Only prefork has the semaphore (concurrency/base.py:68, prefork.py:155); the others get every prefetched request at once, after its last check. In the model (prefork) the window is the hand-off to the child, and after a reconnect, which clears the semaphore, the whole wait for a busy process; that prefork window is not reproduced on the real code. The design checkOnAccept (on_accepted reads the revoked set) passes noRunAfterRevokeKnown and noRunAfterExpiry.
